newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PM Kok may meet Blair this week - media.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PM Kok may meet Blair this week - media.

text.p: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok may travel to London this week for talks with his newly elected British counterpart, Tony Blair, Dutch media said on Monday.
A spokeswoman for Kok's office said she could not confirm or deny the reports that a meeting was being planned by the Dutch government, which holds the EU presidency.
"I can't comment on these reports. There is no official word on it," she said.
News agency ANP said potential talks would focus on EU matters ahead of the key summit on treaty reforms to be held in Amsterdam on June 16-17.
Newspaper De Telegraaf said a meeting would "probably" take place later this week, making Kok the first premier to meet Blair personally.
On Friday Kok congratulated Blair on the Labour Party's landslide win in the British general election and said he hoped the new government would be cooperative on European issues.

The Dutch have also scheduled an informal meeting of EU leaders in Noordwijk on May 23. Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo said on Friday the extra summit would give member states the chance to quiz Blair on his stance towards deeper EU integration.
